claims.text: Controlled sub-solidus annealing enhances short-range order in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Rapid quenching produces alloys lacking pronounced short-range order.
Enhanced short-range order increases spatial fluctuations in local shear-fault energy.
Regions with higher local shear-fault energy act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Increased dislocation pinning delays the onset of plasticity.
Delayed plasticity caused by short-range-order-mediated pinning increases yield strength.
Short-range-order-mediated pinning modifies slip behavior relative to alloys with minimal short-range order.
Annealed alloys with enhanced short-range order will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched alloys.
Annealed alloys with enhanced short-range order will exhibit increased strain hardening relative to rapidly quenched alloys.
Annealed alloys will exhibit distinct dislocation structures and altered slip bands indicating enhanced pinning.
The initial alloys are single-phase solid solutions with significant lattice distortion and chemical complexity.
Sub-solidus annealing can promote short-range order while preserving overall composition and lattice structure.
There is a sub-solidus treatment window in which short-range order develops without phase separation or other microstructural changes.
The proposed effect should hold under temperature and strain-rate conditions where deformation is dominated by dislocation activity.
Simulation and diffraction studies qualitatively support a relationship between short-range order and shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
The quantitative contribution of short-range order and its interplay with inherent lattice distortion remain uncertain.
Samples with identical composition but different thermal histories should be mechanically tested under identical conditions while their short-range order and dislocation structures are characterized.
Failure to observe consistently higher yield strength, altered slip behavior, or increased pinning in the short-range-order-enhanced samples would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as having an identical microstructure, while the comparison requires different short-range order and associated local structural fluctuations. If short-range order is considered part of microstructure, these statements are incompatible; the intended control appears to be identical phase, grain structure, and defect state apart from short-range order.
